name: profile.import
title: Import ConnectorProfiles and Servers
summary: Validate-then-apply: the whole payload is schema-validated and secret-extracted before anything is written, so a malformed or credential-bearing import cannot half-apply. Payloads above the frame limit arrive as envelope.chunk frames and are rejected on any hash or sequence mismatch.

allOf.description: A single-frame import must carry at least one profile or subscription source. Subscription sources declare the owners of URL credentials before subscription.refresh; they remain extension-owned and are not written by the Connector. A chunked import may carry no profiles on slice frames.

A chunked import cannot be verified without the hash of the whole, so contentHash and the slice body are mandatory on every slice frame. Fragment model: each slice carries its fragment of the serialized import document as base64 in `payload`, and `chunk.contentHash` is sha256 over the concatenation of the decoded fragments of the group in chunkSeq order -- the hash of the reassembled bytes, not of any single slice. The Connector rejects a reassembled payload whose hash differs (IntegrityMismatch) rather than importing an unknown subset. The slice fields are nested under `chunk` -- the same shape protocol/envelope.schema.json#/properties/chunk uses for the frame carrying this call; that object is authoritative and scripts/verify.mjs asserts this mirror is structurally identical to it. Group rules the same script enforces over protocol/fixtures/protocol/*.jsonl: every slice of one import (same envelope.id) declares the same chunkCount, its chunkSeq values cover 0..chunkCount-1 exactly once, args.contentHash equals args.chunk.contentHash, and the reassembled `payload` fragments hash to the declared contentHash; a group that disagrees about contentHash must be answered by IntegrityMismatch.

The slice body exists only on a chunked frame. A single-frame import carries its document in `profiles`, `servers` and `subscriptions` directly; a `payload` beside a frame that does not declare `chunk` has no reassembly to belong to and is rejected rather than ignored.

A credential never travels on a chunked frame. A slice is reassembled in the extension's import-staging namespace, which lives in chrome.storage.local and is protected by nothing but its expiry -- so a value split across slices would sit in the one buffer DPAPI does not reach (docs/architecture/32 §6). The payload that carries `credentials` MUST arrive whole in a single frame, which is why the field is bounded at 512 entries and each value at 4 KiB: hand-entered material and a legacy backup's auth maps both fit, a feed body does not and must not be here.

subscriptions.description: Public source documents declaring owners of URL credentials. They are validated but never stored by the Connector; the full private address arrives only in credentials and the public url carries a redacted display address.

payload.description: The slice body: a base64 fragment of the serialized import document, one fragment per chunked frame. The reassembled bytes are a UTF-8 JSON object shaped like a single-frame `profile.import` args without `chunk`, `payload`, `contentHash` and `credentials` -- the profiles, servers, subscriptions and mode the command applies -- and the Connector validates each field against the same schema this command references before anything is written. Required on a chunked frame and forbidden beside a frame without `chunk` (the second and fourth allOf clauses). `chunk.contentHash` is sha256 over the concatenation of the decoded fragments of the group in chunkSeq order; the `encoding: "base64"` member names exactly this arrangement.

chunk.description: Mirror of protocol/envelope.schema.json#/properties/chunk for the frame carrying this slice: same four fields, nested under `chunk`, with the values the envelope copy carries. The object is slice metadata only -- the fragment itself rides in `payload`. The Connector echoes it so the caller can verify completeness. Constrained field-by-field by the allOf above when present; a frame whose envelope `chunk` and `args.chunk` disagree is rejected, not reconciled.

backupBeforeWrite.description: Not optional. A destructive import mode must be preceded by a verified snapshot on both sides (docs/architecture/35-schema-versioning-migration.md §7, §11).

credentials.description: The keystore write primitive, and the only place in the entire command surface where secret material may arrive as a value instead of a reference. It exists for exactly two cases: a credential the user typed (a VLESS UUID, a header value, a token), and a legacy ZeroOmega backup whose 'auth' and 'headers' fields are values that no reference could have replaced on the way in. Everything a subscription can carry arrives through `subscription.refresh`, which fetches and parses inside the Connector, so its values never cross the pipe (docs/architecture/29 §2). The Connector writes each entry to the keystore, mints or confirms its reference, and drops the value: it is not in the result, not in any log line, not in the idempotency record (ADR-0008 stores responses, never requests), and the only thing this command says about it is the count -- `result.secretsExtracted`. Re-sending the same entity and field with a new value overwrites, which is credential rotation. Forbidden on a chunked frame (the third `allOf` clause): a reassembly buffer lives in the extension's import-staging namespace, where DPAPI does not reach.

entity.description: Which class owns the secret. Mirrors the entity set in envelope-keys.schema.json#/properties/secretReferences; scripts/verify.mjs fails if the two lists separate.

entityId.description: The owning entity's identifier, or a prefix of it. The Connector resolves it against the entities in this same payload and refuses an entry whose owner does not exist -- an orphaned credential is a failure, not a stash.

field.description: Which field of the entity this is, from the closed vocabulary in envelope-keys.schema.json#/properties/secretReferences. It is what the minted reference ends with, so a new kind of secret is a schema change, not an invented string.

value.description: The secret itself. `headers` is the one field whose value is a map rather than a string. Declared writeOnly because a value that may arrive MUST NOT leave: no result schema field, fixture or diagnostics section may echo it back.

backupKeys.description: Extension-side '-nexora.backup.<iso>' key and Connector-side snapshot path id. Both MUST be restorable.

secretsExtracted.description: Count of `credentials` entries this command moved into the keystore -- the only statement it makes about them. Zero for a subscription-sourced import: `subscription.refresh` parses inside the Connector and writes the keystore there, so no value ever crosses the pipe (docs/architecture/29 §2). Non-zero only where the user or a legacy backup supplied values through `args.credentials`, which is the single ingest path in this surface (docs/architecture/32 §6). A payload that still contains a value in an entity field after this command ran is a SecretRedacted failure, not a stripped document.

invariants: mode 'replace' MUST be atomic: on any rejection nothing is written, so a user does not lose working profiles to a partially valid file.
an entry in credentials whose entityId names no entity in the same payload is refused; a secret that nothing references is a failure, not a stash, because no later purge path can reach it.
